title: Nicest Office Buildings in San Francisco: Premium Spaces | Tandem
summary: Discover San Francisco's nicest office buildings, from Salesforce Tower to Jackson Square, what premium space costs, and how a startup can lease it.
body_markdown:
San Francisco's nicest office buildings range from Salesforce Tower, the city's tallest, to the 1920s landmarks of the Financial District and the brick lofts of Jackson Square. Asking rents in these buildings vary widely, from roughly $70–$80 per square foot per year at the low end to well above $140 for the best floors, with trophy towers like Salesforce Tower and 555 California at the top of that range. That's far above the $46 citywide median for startup-sized suites in Tandem's[H1 2026 SF Market Report](https://tandemspace.com/blog/san-francisco-office-market-report-h1-2026) . This guide covers which buildings and neighborhoods stand out, what premium space actually costs, and how a growing startup can lease it.


## What Makes an Office Building "Nice"?


Ask a law firm and a Series A startup to name the nicest office building in San Francisco and you'll get different answers. 44% of Tandem's clients asked for a loft or industrial aesthetic rather than a tower, and 62% asked for windows with direct natural light. For founders, the best buildings tend to check these boxes:


- **Light and views** : Floor-to-ceiling windows, high floors, or skylit lofts. In a city with this much fog, natural light is a real differentiator.
- **Transit** : BART or Muni within a five-minute walk, which 52% of SF founders asked for. Buildings near the Montgomery and Embarcadero stations or the Salesforce Transit Center make commuting from the East Bay and the Peninsula easier.
- **Character or polish** : Either a building with history, like a 1920s tower or a brick warehouse, or a modern Class A tower with a strong lobby and amenities.
- **Outdoor space** : Roof decks, terraces, and nearby parks like Salesforce Park matter more in San Francisco's mild climate than almost anywhere else.
- **Seismic readiness** : Ask whether older buildings have completed seismic retrofits. Newer towers were built to modern codes.
- **Room to grow** : 85% of SF founders asked for space to double their headcount in the same suite, so buildings with a range of suite sizes make it easier to expand without moving.


## Which San Francisco Neighborhoods Have the Nicest Office Buildings?


### Financial District


The[Financial District](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/fidi) holds San Francisco's most recognizable towers, including 555 California, the Transamerica Pyramid, and 101 California, alongside historic landmarks like the Russ Building. It's also where Tandem sees the most search activity and the most inventory for small teams. Typical startup-sized space runs $45–$55 per square foot, while premium towers start around $70–$80 per square foot and can run well above $140.


### South Financial District


South of Market Street, the[South Financial District](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/south-fidi) around the Salesforce Transit Center is home to the city's newest towers: Salesforce Tower, 181 Fremont, 555 Mission, and 535 Mission. Expect about $55–$75 per square foot for "average" space here, with top floors in the tallest towers asking far more.


### Embarcadero


The[Embarcadero](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/embarcadero) combines waterfront views with some of the city's largest office complexes. The four Embarcadero Center towers dominate, and the Ferry Building and One Market Plaza add historic waterfront options. Space here typically runs $50–$60 per square foot, but small-team inventory is limited because large institutional landlords own most of it.


### Jackson Square


[Jackson Square](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/jackson-square) is the city's boutique alternative: 19th-century brick buildings, small floor plates, and a quiet, historic feel. It has the highest rents among core startup neighborhoods, typically $55–$65 per square foot, and supply is tight because established law and finance firms tend to stay on long leases.


### SoMa, Mission Bay, and Dogpatch


If "nicest" means a converted warehouse with exposed brick and big windows, look at[SoMa](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/soma) ($38–$50 per square foot), or[Dogpatch](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/dogpatch) and[Mission Bay](https://tandemspace.com/offices/san-francisco/mission-bay) . Dogpatch and Mission Bay draw strong interest but have very little startup-sized supply, so many teams end up in SoMa or the Mission instead.


## Which San Francisco Office Buildings Are the Nicest?


These buildings come up most often when founders ask for San Francisco's best office space.


### Salesforce Tower (415 Mission Street)


At 1,070 feet and 61 floors, Salesforce Tower has been San Francisco's tallest building since it was completed in 2018. It sits next to the Salesforce Transit Center and its rooftop Salesforce Park, with sweeping bay views from the upper floors.


### 555 California Street


The former Bank of America Center was San Francisco's tallest building when it opened in 1969, at 779 feet. Its dark granite facade makes it one of the most recognizable towers in the Financial District.


### Transamerica Pyramid (600 Montgomery Street)


The 853-foot, 48-floor pyramid has defined the skyline since 1972. A recent renovation by Foster + Partners added tenant amenity floors with a fitness center, a lounge, and meeting rooms.


### Embarcadero Center


Designed by John Portman and built in the 1970s, Embarcadero Center's four connected office towers, the tallest at 45 stories, sit above a shopping and dining podium a block from the Ferry Building. BXP has owned the complex since 1998. It's one of the most active premium buildings on Tandem, partially due to the number of units available and the ability to grow into larger suites over time.


### 101 California Street


Philip Johnson and John Burgee's faceted glass cylinder rises 600 feet over a seven-story glass lobby and granite plaza. Completed in 1982, its 48 floors offer some of the most distinctive views in the Financial District.


### 555 Mission Street


Completed in 2008, this 33-story tower was the first speculative office building in San Francisco to earn LEED Gold. Its floor plates step down from about 20,700 to 16,000 square feet as the tower rises.


### 181 Fremont


One of the city's newest towers, 181 Fremont rises 802 feet including its spire and was completed in 2018. Offices fill floors 3 through 38, with residences above. Listings here are infrequent, so it's worth watching for subleases.


### 535 Mission and 101 Second Street


These Transbay towers are among the most frequently listed premium buildings on Tandem. Recent listings have asked a median of $75+ per square foot, a middle ground between the newest trophy towers and older buildings.


### The Ferry Building and One Market Plaza


Above the Ferry Building's 1898 marketplace, the second and third floors hold about 175,000 square feet of offices with direct waterfront access. Next door, One Market Plaza adds larger floors overlooking the bay. Small-team listings are rare in both, so it pays to watch for subleases.


### Levi's Plaza


Built in 1981 as Levi Strauss & Co.'s headquarters, Levi's Plaza is the only large-scale office campus in San Francisco's central business district: nine buildings on 9.4 acres around a Lawrence Halprin-designed plaza and park at the foot of Telegraph Hill.


### The Russ Building (235 Montgomery Street)


Completed in 1927, the 32-story Neo-Gothic Russ Building was San Francisco's tallest building until 1964 and is a California Historical Landmark. Its marble and granite lobbies give it real character, and it's typically one of the more affordable options on this list.


## What Do the Nicest Office Buildings in San Francisco Actually Cost?


Pricing in San Francisco's top buildings varies too much for a single number to be useful. As a rule of thumb, expect asking rents from about $70–$80 per square foot per year at the low end to well above $140 for the best floors, with trophy towers like Salesforce Tower and 555 California at the top of that range. Direct leases in these buildings almost always run at least three years.


**What moves the price within that range:**


- **Floor and view** : Top floors with bay views command the highest rents.
- **The building itself** : Trophy towers price above older or renovated towers, even a block away.
- **Suite condition** : A built-out, move-in-ready suite costs more than space taken as-is.
- **Term and timing** : A longer commitment, or a suite that has sat vacant for a while, leaves more room to negotiate.
- **Subleases** : Often priced below direct rents in the same building, on a shorter fixed term.

For context, Tandem's[H1 2026 SF Market Report](https://tandemspace.com/blog/san-francisco-office-market-report-h1-2026) puts the citywide median for startup-sized suites at $46 per square foot, with core startup neighborhoods between $38 and $65. The buildings in this guide are the top of the market.


For sizing, use 150 square feet per person. A 10-person team needs about 1,500 square feet, which at $70–$140 per square foot works out to roughly $8,750–$17,500 a month in rent, and more on the best floors. Larger teams often get better value: Tandem's data puts all-in costs at $462 per person per month for teams of 21–50, compared with $746–$828 for smaller teams, partly because larger floor plates are in lower demand.


Security deposits in San Francisco typically run 2–3 months' rent. For how building classes compare, see[Class A, B, and C office space](https://tandemspace.com/blog/class-a-office-space) .


## Amenities Worth Paying For (and What to Confirm Before You Sign)


**Building-level amenities (worth paying for):**


- Roof decks, terraces, or direct access to parks like Salesforce Park
- A staffed lobby and 24/7 secure access
- Fitness centers, bike storage, and showers for bike commuters
- Tenant lounges and bookable conference floors, now common in renovated towers like the Transamerica Pyramid


**Infrastructure (non-negotiable):**


- Fiber from multiple providers already in the building
- HVAC hours and overtime rates: after-hours HVAC typically costs $150–$400 an hour in large Class A towers and $50–$150 in smaller buildings
- Seismic retrofit status for older buildings
- Freight elevator access for your move-in


## How to Get Space in San Francisco's Best Office Buildings


The nicest buildings in San Francisco rarely show up on generic listing sites. Most premium inventory moves through landlord brokers and relationships, which is why a tenant rep broker matters here. A typical process for a private lease:


1. **Define your requirements** : headcount in 12 months, size, budget, neighborhoods, and term.
2. **Tour 4–5 spaces in a single day** : most SF companies who use Tandem sign after one tour day.
3. **Submit a letter of intent (LOI)** : it covers rent, term, deposit, and improvements.
4. **Negotiate the lease** : in premium buildings, push on free rent, improvements, and personal guarantee terms.
5. **Sign and move in** : through Tandem, SF startups typically take 27 days from first tour to signed lease.


For a full walkthrough of each step, see[How to Lease Office Space](https://tandemspace.com/how-to-lease-office-space) .


## Alternatives to a Direct Lease in a Premium Building


### Subleases in Premium Towers


Direct leases in top towers almost always run at least three years, and landlords in buildings like Salesforce Tower can push for longer on full floors. Subleases let a startup into the same buildings on a shorter, fixed term, often with furniture already in place. Landlord consent is required, so build 2–4 weeks into your timeline.


### Shared Spaces in Premium Buildings


Some companies with extra room in a great building share part of their floor with one or two smaller teams. You get a private, dedicated section of the floor on a simpler agreement, often month to month or with a term of a few months to a year. It's one of the fastest ways into a premium building.


## What to Watch Out for in a Premium San Francisco Building


- **Long terms** : Direct leases in these towers almost always run at least three years, and often longer. Across Tandem's private-office deals, the median term is 17 months, so expect to negotiate or look at subleases.
- **Large floor plates** : Many towers were built for big tenants. Ask for a suite that fits your 12-month headcount rather than taking extra space you'll pay for.
- **After-hours HVAC** : Overtime in large towers can run $150–$400 an hour. Get the schedule and rate in writing.
- **Rentable vs. usable square feet** : Older towers often have high loss factors, so a suite can feel smaller than its listed size. Always walk the space.
- **Aging building systems** : Older landmarks are beautiful but can have dated systems. Ask about seismic retrofits, elevators, and the age of the HVAC.
- **The street-level experience** : Visit at different times of day. The block around a building affects how your team feels about coming in.


## Where to Start Your Search


San Francisco's nicest office buildings are concentrated in the Financial District, the Transbay area, the Embarcadero, and Jackson Square. With rents reset from their pre-pandemic highs, many of them are more accessible to startups than they've been in years.
